meta.content_method: M19 transfer-derived guided work + M25 context-derived oral and independent task prompts; shared scaffolding; not independent human editorial verification.
meta.model_limitation: One M19 model reused as language reference three times for each lesson; speaking/independent tasks need new context-specific models.
meta.grading_limitation: Open-ended tasks never automatically marked incorrect or mastery; no ASR/audio/pronunciation assessment.

People involved in the work have been asked not to circulate an unverified final timetable. On Thursday, the traffic engineer counted 31 collision reports at the city transport unit. A larger headline total would not, on its own, prove that either procedure was more effective. In particular, the team will retain the source of each figure, the date it was recorded and any assumptions used in the comparison. This prevents subsequent readers from confusing a documented observation with an interpretation produced during the meeting. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully.

tasks.source_context_en: A decision memorandum concerning a terminology review has prompted a discussion about what the underlying records can actually support. The day-to-day arrangements for a terminology review are being coordinated by the language specialist. As the planning notes make clear, legal terms have context-sensitive meanings. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the language specialist counted 22 translation drafts at the translation office. Hardly had the meeting begun when the discrepancy emerged. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The central difficulty concerns scope. Evidence about a single group may support a narrow recommendation but does not license a claim about all comparable groups. The revision must preserve that limitation even when stronger phrasing would sound more persuasive. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about legal terms have context-sensitive meanings requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

The transport authority had spent heavily on advertising, but the survey did not isolate any separate effect of those adverts. The evaluators weighted the responses before comparing the periods, but they did not run an experiment capable of proving that the timetable caused all reported changes.

tasks.source_context_en: The review group has been asked to clarify whether the provisional findings about a public-information experiment warrant any policy change. The communications evaluator has asked the team to record both confirmed arrangements and unresolved questions about a public-information experiment. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. According to the internal update, volunteers were not blinded. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Saturday, the communications evaluator counted 36 message variants at the policy unit. Never has the group described the findings as final. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The evidence trail includes an internal log and an unverified participant statement. These are not interchangeable forms of support: the former documents recorded activity, whereas the latter offers an interpretation that may be useful but remains contestable. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully. In this case, the unresolved concern about volunteers were not blinded requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: The archive recently acquired two letters written by a textile worker during the 1930s. The letters describe working conditions in detail; the writer's private family life, however, remains largely undocumented. Of particular interest to historians is a brief reference to a wage dispute, though the archive cannot establish how widely that dispute spread. The editor wants to bring the wage reference to the front of the paragraph without implying that the surviving letters provide a complete account of the factory. One letter includes a date but lacks the name of the person to whom it was sent. The catalogue therefore records the probable recipient separately from verified details, allowing future historians to revise that inference without rewriting the factual description.

tasks.source_context_en: A committee received its supporting documents only after an important meeting had ended. A retrospective report sets out the procedural shortcoming without falsely implying the papers were sent on time. The documents should have been sent before the meeting. The meeting finished at four on Tuesday. The secretary is not asserting that the delay alone changed the decision. Nonetheless, earlier circulation would have given participants more time to examine the evidence and raise questions. One committee member had asked for the materials a week earlier, yet the records team was waiting for permission to distribute an appendix. A counterfactual modal passive expresses a procedural obligation that was not met, not evidence that the documents actually arrived.

tasks.source_context_en: The review group has been asked to clarify whether the provisional findings about a procurement disclosure review warrant any policy change. The legal adviser has asked the team to record both confirmed arrangements and unresolved questions about a procurement disclosure review. According to the internal update, some prices include different service bundles. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the legal adviser counted 32 bid records at the procurement board. Never has the group described the findings as final. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The evidence trail includes an internal log and an unverified participant statement. These are not interchangeable forms of support: the former documents recorded activity, whereas the latter offers an interpretation that may be useful but remains contestable. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully. In this case, the unresolved concern about some prices include different service bundles requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: An editorial committee is revising a briefing on a breach-reporting assessment so that certainty and attribution are not overstated. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. The editorial review treats that as a substantive error of attribution, not merely an awkward choice of words. Responsibility must remain with the body actually named in the record. One participant recalled a different sequence of events, yet the written log is the only record agreed by the team. In this case, the unresolved concern about several incidents lack confirmation requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: A cross-departmental assessment of a conservation genetics study distinguishes established observations from claims requiring confirmation. The field geneticist is drafting the next update about a conservation genetics study without assuming that earlier suggestions were formally accepted. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. The available record includes one qualification: sites were sampled at unequal intervals. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Saturday, the field geneticist counted 46 sequence samples at the biodiversity centre. What matters most is the basis of the claim. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Thursday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. A rapid response was proposed, but the committee declined to equate urgency with certainty. Its revised account identifies the conditions under which a change could be justified and notes which measurements have yet to be corroborated. The project team received a second request after the count, but that request is not included in the current total. In this case, the unresolved concern about sites were sampled at unequal intervals requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

Their brief acknowledges that such differences may partly explain the association, even after buildings with similar floor areas have been compared.

tasks.source_context_en: A decision memorandum concerning an equity-monitoring review has prompted a discussion about what the underlying records can actually support. Responsibility for the current review of an equity-monitoring review rests with the assessment specialist, rather than with an outside authority. An important limitation in the current arrangements is that demographic groups differ in background factors. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Monday, the assessment specialist counted 16 student outcomes at the education ministry. Hardly had the meeting begun when the discrepancy emerged. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Tuesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The central difficulty concerns scope. Evidence about a single group may support a narrow recommendation but does not license a claim about all comparable groups. The revision must preserve that limitation even when stronger phrasing would sound more persuasive. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about demographic groups differ in background factors requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: A decision memorandum concerning a bilingual teaching review has prompted a discussion about what the underlying records can actually support. The day-to-day arrangements for a bilingual teaching review are being coordinated by the policy researcher. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Saturday, the policy researcher counted 14 classroom observations at the education council. Hardly had the meeting begun when the discrepancy emerged. Evidence about a single group may support a narrow recommendation but does not license a claim about all comparable groups. The revision must preserve that limitation even when stronger phrasing would sound more persuasive. The preliminary record covers only the activity described here and should not be generalised to every site. In this case, the unresolved concern about the sample excludes remote schools requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

The written record mentions a practical concern: the jurisdictional boundaries are unsettled. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Monday, the legal rapporteur counted 34 compliance submissions at the oversight commission. Had the panel examined the missing records earlier, it might have identified the discrepancy sooner. Instead, she preserved the established ordering of events and identified the unknown interval.

The expert witness is responsible for checking the supporting records before a new decision about a causation assessment is announced. The organisers have drawn attention to the fact that unmeasured confounding remains plausible. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the expert witness counted 18 epidemiological summaries at the inquiry panel. The decision was postponed pending further evidence, not cancelled. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. Two apparently consistent accounts rely on different definitions of completion. Unless those definitions are reconciled, neither account should be used to authorise an irreversible action. The present note deliberately stops short of treating disagreement about terminology as proof of misconduct. The project team received a second request after the count, but that request is not included in the current total. In this case, the unresolved concern about unmeasured confounding remains plausible requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

On Friday, the appeals convenor counted 30 appeal statements at the ethics tribunal. Had the panel examined the missing records earlier, it might have identified the discrepancy sooner. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Wednesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The strongest admissible reading is narrower than the first draft implied. Both distinctions affect the institutional implications of the statement. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked. In this case, the unresolved concern about the appellant challenges the sampling method requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: A specialist panel is drafting a qualified assessment of a synthesis review in response to conflicting interpretations of the record. For a synthesis review, the synthesis author is comparing the current plan with the written record. The purpose of this note is to help readers distinguish the event itself from the decisions that may follow. The team has not yet resolved a specific concern: minority findings require careful representation. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Thursday, the synthesis author counted 28 consensus drafts at the research council. Had the panel examined the missing records earlier, it might have identified the discrepancy sooner. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Saturday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. The strongest admissible reading is narrower than the first draft implied. A chronological association does not establish that the earlier event caused the later one, and an internal observation does not carry the authority of an external adjudication. Both distinctions affect the institutional implications of the statement. A separate note contains a visitor suggestion, but it has not been independently checked. In this case, the unresolved concern about minority findings require careful representation requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: A newsroom correction concerns a statement that a researcher allegedly withheld results from a review panel. The original article's subject position drew attention to the researcher, leaving the absence of evidence in a secondary clause. Subsequent checks showed that the results had been filed but indexed under a different project code. The correction should place the filing error first and name the person only where necessary. This change of information structure does not excuse withholding; it reflects the fact that withholding was not established at all. The correction will be displayed next to the archived article and linked from the updated version. The editor hopes that putting the verified filing facts first will make readers less likely to confuse an administrative classification error with a refusal to disclose information.

tasks.source_context_en: The review of an amendment interpretation has exposed a tension between what can be stated categorically and what remains inferential. The legal scholar has asked the team to record both confirmed arrangements and unresolved questions about an amendment interpretation. According to the internal update, the proposed wording has multiple plausible readings. Several people offered suggestions, but no one has checked whether those suggestions would work in every situation. On Friday, the legal scholar counted 35 briefing papers at the constitutional commission. It is not the case that every proposal was rejected. The team has written a short explanation of the count so that the next reviewer can check how the information was collected. The proposed change is still being reviewed; no final approval has been issued. The final review is scheduled for Wednesday. The internal team, not an external regulator, prepared this preliminary assessment. A cautious formulation is not a rhetorical weakness here. It is the only formulation warranted by the record as it stands: some evidence is contemporaneous, some retrospective, and some is absent altogether. The editor must avoid collapsing those categories into a single purportedly conclusive account. The draft spreadsheet contains an older figure, which explains why the revised number must be quoted carefully. In this case, the unresolved concern about the proposed wording has multiple plausible readings requires further checks before a general conclusion can be drawn. A statement that presents this concern as an established cause would exceed the available evidence.

tasks.source_context_en: An audit summary compares two hospital wards that introduced different appointment reminder systems. Missed appointments fell on both wards, but the report did not control for seasonal staffing changes. One draft paragraph called the intervention a proven cause of the decline and then used this success to justify a separate claim about patient satisfaction, which the audit never measured. The editor's job is to repair the logical chain, keep the observed reduction in missed visits, and remove causal or experiential claims unsupported by the data. Clear cohesion should make the evidential boundary easier, not harder, to see. The report's limitations section also notes different appointment types and changes in staff availability across the wards. Without a suitable comparison design, those differences are plausible alternative explanations, not details that may be omitted for a smoother narrative conclusion.

(1) Không tự thêm sự kiện/tác nhân/nguyên nhân; (2) quan hệ thời gian, phạm vi phủ định và độ chắc chắn nhất quán; (3) lựa chọn cấu trúc tạo hiệu quả thực sự về register/cohesion; (4) không có tham chiếu mơ hồ; (5) giải thích được hai quyết định biên tập. Có nhiều đáp án hợp lệ; ví dụ chỉ để đối chiếu.
